blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 2.10
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 2.10

blocks.text: विद्यासंहारे तदुत्थस्वप्नदर्शनम्
blocks.directed: [slowly] विद्यासंहारे तदुत्थस्वप्नदर्शनम्

blocks.text: Vidyāsaṃhāre tadutthasvapnadarśanam.
blocks.directed: Vidyāsaṃhāre tadutthasvapnadarśanam.

blocks.text: When pure knowledge subsides, the dreamlike appearances arising from its fading become visible again.
blocks.directed: When pure knowledge subsides, the dreamlike appearances arising from its fading become visible again.

blocks.text: You Realise You’re Śiva, Then Immediately Forget Again Like an Absolute Idiot.
blocks.directed: You Realise You’re Śiva, Then Immediately Forget Again Like an Absolute Idiot.

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Right.

blocks.text: This final sūtra is absolutely devastating.
blocks.directed: This final sūtra is absolutely devastating.

blocks.text: And honestly, perhaps the most relatable statement in the entire second book.
blocks.directed: And honestly, perhaps the most relatable statement in the entire second book.

blocks.text: Because after all this extraordinary metaphysics, after the divine mantra, after the awakening of Mātṛkā, after the sacrifice of the body, after the devouring of differentiated knowledge—
blocks.directed: Because after all this extraordinary metaphysics, after the divine mantra, after the awakening of Mātṛkā, after the sacrifice of the body, after the devouring of differentiated knowledge—

blocks.text: Vasugupta says:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Vasugupta says:

blocks.text: You might forget.
blocks.directed: You might forget.

blocks.text: That’s it.
blocks.directed: That’s it.

blocks.text: You’ve recognised the truth.
blocks.directed: You’ve recognised the truth.

blocks.text: You’ve understood the fundamental nature of consciousness.
blocks.directed: You’ve understood the fundamental nature of consciousness.

blocks.text: You’ve experienced the dissolution of limited identification.
blocks.directed: You’ve experienced the dissolution of limited identification.

blocks.text: You’ve seen the world as the manifestation of Śakti.
blocks.directed: You’ve seen the world as the manifestation of Śakti.

blocks.text: And then…
blocks.directed: And then…

blocks.text: Someone sends you an annoying message.
blocks.directed: Someone sends you an annoying message.

blocks.text: Suddenly you’re back.
blocks.directed: Suddenly you’re back.

blocks.text: “I cannot BELIEVE this person.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “I cannot BELIEVE this person.”

blocks.text: “How dare they.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “How dare they.”

blocks.text: “Do they not appreciate who they’re dealing with?”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Do they not appreciate who they’re dealing with?”

blocks.text: And just like that, the individual identity has returned to centre stage.
blocks.directed: And just like that, the individual identity has returned to centre stage.

blocks.text: The cosmic drama has resumed.
blocks.directed: The cosmic drama has resumed.

blocks.text: Śiva has once again become a bloke arguing with his phone.
blocks.directed: Śiva has once again become a bloke arguing with his phone.

blocks.text: Now, obviously, this is a modern psychological illustration.
blocks.directed: Now, obviously, this is a modern psychological illustration.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja’s actual discussion is more technical.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja’s actual discussion is more technical.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Vidyā — knowledge, here pure liberating knowledge.
blocks.directed: Vidyā — knowledge, here pure liberating knowledge.

blocks.text: Saṃhāra — withdrawal, subsidence, disappearance.
blocks.directed: Saṃhāra — withdrawal, subsidence, disappearance.

blocks.text: Taduttha — arising from that, or resulting from it.
blocks.directed: Taduttha — arising from that, or resulting from it.

blocks.text: Svapna — dream.
blocks.directed: Svapna — dream.

blocks.text: Darśana — seeing, appearance.
blocks.directed: Darśana — seeing, appearance.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja describes what happens when the practitioner’s attention to pure knowledge weakens.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja describes what happens when the practitioner’s attention to pure knowledge weakens.

blocks.text: The awareness of supreme reality is no longer maintained.
blocks.directed: The awareness of supreme reality is no longer maintained.

blocks.text: The impressions of that awareness gradually fade.
blocks.directed: The impressions of that awareness gradually fade.

blocks.text: And the differentiated mental world reasserts itself.
blocks.directed: And the differentiated mental world reasserts itself.

blocks.text: The svapna here isn’t necessarily a literal dream during sleep.
blocks.directed: The svapna here isn’t necessarily a literal dream during sleep.

blocks.text: It is the dreamlike manifestation of limited, differentiated cognition.
blocks.directed: It is the dreamlike manifestation of limited, differentiated cognition.

blocks.text: The world once again appears in terms of subject and object, possession and loss, attraction and aversion.
blocks.directed: The world once again appears in terms of subject and object, possession and loss, attraction and aversion.

blocks.text: And the yogi can become caught up in those distinctions.
blocks.directed: And the yogi can become caught up in those distinctions.

blocks.text: Now here’s something very important.
blocks.directed: Now here’s something very important.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja is not saying Śiva has literally stopped existing.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja is not saying Śiva has literally stopped existing.

blocks.text: Or that universal consciousness has somehow disappeared.
blocks.directed: Or that universal consciousness has somehow disappeared.

blocks.text: That would contradict the basic doctrine.
blocks.directed: That would contradict the basic doctrine.

blocks.text: Rather, the recognition of pure consciousness has subsided for the practitioner.
blocks.directed: Rather, the recognition of pure consciousness has subsided for the practitioner.

blocks.text: The underlying reality has not changed.
blocks.directed: The underlying reality has not changed.

blocks.text: The mode of awareness has changed.
blocks.directed: The mode of awareness has changed.

blocks.text: This is the heart of the issue.
blocks.directed: This is the heart of the issue.

blocks.text: You see clearly.
blocks.directed: You see clearly.

blocks.text: Then you become distracted.
blocks.directed: Then you become distracted.

blocks.text: Then you remember.
blocks.directed: Then you remember.

blocks.text: Then you become absorbed in something else.
blocks.directed: Then you become absorbed in something else.

blocks.text: Then you recognise again.
blocks.directed: Then you recognise again.

blocks.text: A continual alternation of recognition and contraction.
blocks.directed: A continual alternation of recognition and contraction.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja is concerned with what happens when awareness lacks the steadiness necessary for sustained recognition.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja is concerned with what happens when awareness lacks the steadiness necessary for sustained recognition.

blocks.text: He invokes the Mālinīvijayatantra and Spandakārikā to explain that even a genuine opening can be followed by renewed involvement in differentiated experience.
blocks.directed: He invokes the Mālinīvijayatantra and Spandakārikā to explain that even a genuine opening can be followed by renewed involvement in differentiated experience.

blocks.text: The latent impressions of recognition may remain, but attention is no longer established in their source. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: The latent impressions of recognition may remain, but attention is no longer established in their source. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: And this is why the sūtra is a warning.
blocks.directed: And this is why the sūtra is a warning.

blocks.text: Not because the world is inherently evil.
blocks.directed: Not because the world is inherently evil.

blocks.text: Not because ordinary experience is something to hate.
blocks.directed: Not because ordinary experience is something to hate.

blocks.text: But because the yogi may become identified once more with the limitations appearing within experience.
blocks.directed: But because the yogi may become identified once more with the limitations appearing within experience.

blocks.text: Consider what happens when someone understands a profound philosophical truth.
blocks.directed: Consider what happens when someone understands a profound philosophical truth.

blocks.text: For a moment, everything is clear.
blocks.directed: For a moment, everything is clear.

blocks.text: You see how all the elements fit together.
blocks.directed: You see how all the elements fit together.

blocks.text: You understand the problem.
blocks.directed: You understand the problem.

blocks.text: You feel an extraordinary freedom from the confusion that previously occupied you.
blocks.directed: You feel an extraordinary freedom from the confusion that previously occupied you.

blocks.text: And then, a few hours later, you find yourself behaving as though none of that understanding had ever happened.
blocks.directed: And then, a few hours later, you find yourself behaving as though none of that understanding had ever happened.

blocks.text: The knowledge was real at the level at which it occurred.
blocks.directed: The knowledge was real at the level at which it occurred.

blocks.text: But it had not become stable.
blocks.directed: But it had not become stable.

blocks.text: This is a useful analogy for what Kṣemarāja is discussing, though the actual sūtra concerns a much more profound yogic recognition than an intellectual insight.
blocks.directed: This is a useful analogy for what Kṣemarāja is discussing, though the actual sūtra concerns a much more profound yogic recognition than an intellectual insight.

blocks.text: The important point is stabilisation.
blocks.directed: The important point is stabilisation.

blocks.text: Not merely having recognised.
blocks.directed: Not merely having recognised.

blocks.text: But remaining established in recognition.
blocks.directed: But remaining established in recognition.

blocks.text: And here Kṣemarāja provides the transition to the next section.
blocks.directed: And here Kṣemarāja provides the transition to the next section.

blocks.text: If the practitioner cannot maintain the attentive recognition characteristic of Śāktopāya, another form of practice becomes appropriate.
blocks.directed: If the practitioner cannot maintain the attentive recognition characteristic of Śāktopāya, another form of practice becomes appropriate.

blocks.text: One employing more concrete supports.
blocks.directed: One employing more concrete supports.

blocks.text: More articulated procedures.
blocks.directed: More articulated procedures.

blocks.text: More deliberate engagement with the faculties of the limited individual.
blocks.directed: More deliberate engagement with the faculties of the limited individual.

blocks.text: And thus, the third book emerges.
blocks.directed: And thus, the third book emerges.

blocks.text: Āṇavopāya.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Āṇavopāya.

blocks.text: The way of the aṇu.
blocks.directed: The way of the aṇu.

blocks.text: The limited individual.
blocks.directed: The limited individual.

blocks.text: Where the teaching begins working with the very structures through which consciousness experiences itself as finite.
blocks.directed: Where the teaching begins working with the very structures through which consciousness experiences itself as finite.

blocks.text: Which is a rather beautiful conclusion.
blocks.directed: Which is a rather beautiful conclusion.

blocks.text: Because even when the practitioner becomes distracted from the highest recognition, the tradition doesn’t simply abandon them.
blocks.directed: Because even when the practitioner becomes distracted from the highest recognition, the tradition doesn’t simply abandon them.

blocks.text: There remains another way.
blocks.directed: There remains another way.

blocks.text: The capacity for practice belongs to the same Śakti.
blocks.directed: The capacity for practice belongs to the same Śakti.

blocks.text: The limited individual has not fallen outside consciousness.
blocks.directed: The limited individual has not fallen outside consciousness.

blocks.text: They have merely returned to a contracted mode of awareness.
blocks.directed: They have merely returned to a contracted mode of awareness.

blocks.text: And that contracted mode can itself become the starting point for liberation.
blocks.directed: And that contracted mode can itself become the starting point for liberation.

blocks.text: The same Śiva.
blocks.directed: The same Śiva.

blocks.text: The same Śakti.
blocks.directed: The same Śakti.

blocks.text: Another method.
blocks.directed: Another method.

blocks.text: Another opportunity.
blocks.directed: Another opportunity.

blocks.text: Another chance for consciousness to recognise what it never ceased to be.
blocks.directed: Another chance for consciousness to recognise what it never ceased to be.

blocks.text:
The Great Reveal — What Was Śāktopāya Actually Teaching?
Let’s revisit the extraordinary progression of these ten statements.
blocks.directed:
The Great Reveal — What Was Śāktopāya Actually Teaching?
Let’s revisit the extraordinary progression of these ten statements.

blocks.text: In the first book, Vasugupta established the supreme nature of consciousness and described the immediate recognition characteristic of Śāmbhavopāya.
blocks.directed: In the first book, Vasugupta established the supreme nature of consciousness and described the immediate recognition characteristic of Śāmbhavopāya.

blocks.text: But Śāktopāya provides a more articulated account of how mental activity itself can participate in liberation.
blocks.directed: But Śāktopāya provides a more articulated account of how mental activity itself can participate in liberation.

blocks.text: The teaching is not:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The teaching is not:

blocks.text: “Stop thinking and become Śiva.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Stop thinking and become Śiva.”

blocks.text: Nor is it:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Nor is it:

blocks.text: “Think hard enough and manufacture Śiva.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Think hard enough and manufacture Śiva.”

blocks.text: It’s something rather subtler.
blocks.directed: It’s something rather subtler.

blocks.text: Recognise the conscious power from which thought arises, and through which its differentiation becomes manifest.
blocks.directed: Recognise the conscious power from which thought arises, and through which its differentiation becomes manifest.

blocks.text: Consider the structure.
blocks.directed: Consider the structure.

blocks.text: 2.1 — Cittaṃ mantraḥ.
blocks.directed: [slowly] 2.1 — Cittaṃ mantraḥ.

blocks.text: The mind becomes mantra through contemplation of its supreme conscious source.
blocks.directed: The mind becomes mantra through contemplation of its supreme conscious source.

blocks.text: 2.2 — Prayatnaḥ sādhakaḥ.
blocks.directed: [slowly] 2.2 — Prayatnaḥ sādhakaḥ.

blocks.text: Spontaneous, directed effort makes this contemplation effective.
blocks.directed: Spontaneous, directed effort makes this contemplation effective.

blocks.text: 2.3 — Vidyāśarīrasattā mantrarahasyam.
blocks.directed: 2.3 — Vidyāśarīrasattā mantrarahasyam.

blocks.text: The hidden reality of mantra is the living power of nondual consciousness.
blocks.directed: The hidden reality of mantra is the living power of nondual consciousness.

blocks.text: 2.4 — Garbhe cittavikāso ’viśiṣṭavidyāsvapnaḥ.
blocks.directed: 2.4 — Garbhe cittavikāso ’viśiṣṭavidyāsvapnaḥ.

blocks.text: The practitioner must not confuse limited accomplishments and visionary phenomena with supreme knowledge.
blocks.directed: The practitioner must not confuse limited accomplishments and visionary phenomena with supreme knowledge.

blocks.text: 2.5 — Vidyāsamutthāne svābhāvike khecarī śivāvasthā.
blocks.directed: [slowly] 2.5 — Vidyāsamutthāne svābhāvike khecarī śivāvasthā.

blocks.text: When supreme knowledge arises spontaneously, Khecarī, the state of Śiva, is revealed.
blocks.directed: When supreme knowledge arises spontaneously, Khecarī, the state of Śiva, is revealed.

blocks.text: 2.6 — Gurur upāyaḥ.
blocks.directed: 2.6 — Gurur upāyaḥ.

blocks.text: The guru, as genuine instruction and the vehicle of divine grace, is a means of recognition.
blocks.directed: The guru, as genuine instruction and the vehicle of divine grace, is a means of recognition.

blocks.text: 2.7 — Mātṛkācakrasambodhaḥ.
blocks.directed: [slowly] 2.7 — Mātṛkācakrasambodhaḥ.

blocks.text: The practitioner awakens to the divine nature of the entire wheel of phonemic powers.
blocks.directed: The practitioner awakens to the divine nature of the entire wheel of phonemic powers.

blocks.text: 2.8 — Śarīraṃ haviḥ.
blocks.directed: [slowly] 2.8 — Śarīraṃ haviḥ.

blocks.text: Limited bodily identification becomes an offering into the fire of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Limited bodily identification becomes an offering into the fire of consciousness.

blocks.text: 2.9 — Jñānam annam.
blocks.directed: 2.9 — Jñānam annam.

blocks.text: Differentiated knowledge is consumed within nondual recognition.
blocks.directed: Differentiated knowledge is consumed within nondual recognition.

blocks.text: 2.10 — Vidyāsaṃhāre tadutthasvapnadarśanam.
blocks.directed: [slowly] 2.10 — Vidyāsaṃhāre tadutthasvapnadarśanam.

blocks.text: When that recognition subsides, dreamlike differentiation returns, providing the reason for further practice.
blocks.directed: When that recognition subsides, dreamlike differentiation returns, providing the reason for further practice.

blocks.text: And there’s an absolutely beautiful symmetry here.
blocks.directed: And there’s an absolutely beautiful symmetry here.

blocks.text: The first section began:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The first section began:

blocks.text: चैतन्यमात्मा।
blocks.directed: [slowly] चैतन्यमात्मा।

blocks.text: Caitanyam ātmā.
blocks.directed: Caitanyam ātmā.

blocks.text: Consciousness is the Self.
blocks.directed: Consciousness is the Self.

blocks.text: The second section began:
blocks.directed: [short pause] The second section began:

blocks.text: चित्तं मन्त्रः।.
blocks.directed: [slowly] चित्तं मन्त्रः।.

blocks.text: Cittaṃ mantraḥ.
blocks.directed: Cittaṃ mantraḥ.

blocks.text: The mind is mantra.
blocks.directed: The mind is mantra.

blocks.text: And the third section will begin:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And the third section will begin:

blocks.text: आत्मा चित्तम्।
blocks.directed: [slowly] आत्मा चित्तम्।

blocks.text: Ātmā cittam.
blocks.directed: Ātmā cittam.

blocks.text: The individual self is mind.
blocks.directed: The individual self is mind.

blocks.text: Three different points of departure.
blocks.directed: Three different points of departure.

blocks.text: Three distinct approaches to the problem of recognition.
blocks.directed: Three distinct approaches to the problem of recognition.

blocks.text: The supreme standpoint of Śiva.
blocks.directed: The supreme standpoint of Śiva.

blocks.text: The transformative power of Śakti.
blocks.directed: The transformative power of Śakti.

blocks.text: And the limited standpoint of the individual.
blocks.directed: And the limited standpoint of the individual.

blocks.text: All directed towards the recognition of the one conscious reality.
blocks.directed: All directed towards the recognition of the one conscious reality.

blocks.text:
The Final Teaching — You Cannot Escape Śakti
Here’s the extraordinary thing about Śāktopāya.
blocks.directed:
The Final Teaching — You Cannot Escape Śakti
Here’s the extraordinary thing about Śāktopāya.

blocks.text: Everything that appears to separate you from your true nature is itself an expression of the power of that nature.
blocks.directed: Everything that appears to separate you from your true nature is itself an expression of the power of that nature.

blocks.text: Thought.
blocks.directed: Thought.

blocks.text: Language.
blocks.directed: Language.

blocks.text: Desire.
blocks.directed: Desire.

blocks.text: Mental activity.
blocks.directed: Mental activity.

blocks.text: Differentiation.
blocks.directed: Differentiation.

blocks.text: The sense of being an individual.
blocks.directed: The sense of being an individual.

blocks.text: All belong, in the final analysis, to the manifestation of Śakti.
blocks.directed: All belong, in the final analysis, to the manifestation of Śakti.

blocks.text: And therefore, the path to recognition doesn’t always require rejecting them.
blocks.directed: And therefore, the path to recognition doesn’t always require rejecting them.

blocks.text: It can involve understanding them so completely that their conscious source becomes apparent.
blocks.directed: It can involve understanding them so completely that their conscious source becomes apparent.

blocks.text: The same language that articulates limitation can become mantra.
blocks.directed: The same language that articulates limitation can become mantra.

blocks.text: The same mental activity that constructs difference can become contemplative recognition.
blocks.directed: The same mental activity that constructs difference can become contemplative recognition.

blocks.text: The same Mātṛkā that structures differentiated knowledge can disclose the universal I-consciousness.
blocks.directed: The same Mātṛkā that structures differentiated knowledge can disclose the universal I-consciousness.

blocks.text: The same body that appears to define your individuality can become an offering into its conscious source.
blocks.directed: The same body that appears to define your individuality can become an offering into its conscious source.

blocks.text: The same knowledge that constitutes bondage can become food for liberation.
blocks.directed: The same knowledge that constitutes bondage can become food for liberation.

blocks.text: And when recognition disappears?
blocks.directed: And when recognition disappears?

blocks.text: Even that forgetting occurs within the power of consciousness.
blocks.directed: Even that forgetting occurs within the power of consciousness.

blocks.text: It has not created a second reality independent of Śiva.
blocks.directed: It has not created a second reality independent of Śiva.

blocks.text: The extraordinary conclusion is that the path and the apparent obstacle are not made from two fundamentally different substances.
blocks.directed: The extraordinary conclusion is that the path and the apparent obstacle are not made from two fundamentally different substances.

blocks.text: They are different modes of the same divine manifestation.
blocks.directed: They are different modes of the same divine manifestation.

blocks.text: Śakti is not a ladder somebody built so you could climb out of the universe.
blocks.directed: Śakti is not a ladder somebody built so you could climb out of the universe.

blocks.text: She’s the power through which the universe appears.
blocks.directed: She’s the power through which the universe appears.

blocks.text: The power through which you experience yourself as limited.
blocks.directed: The power through which you experience yourself as limited.

blocks.text: And the power through which that limitation can be recognised as a contraction of the infinite.
blocks.directed: And the power through which that limitation can be recognised as a contraction of the infinite.

blocks.text: The Goddess isn’t waiting at the end of the path.
blocks.directed: The Goddess isn’t waiting at the end of the path.

blocks.text: She’s been making the path, walking the path, and appearing as the confused individual wondering where the path leads.
blocks.directed: She’s been making the path, walking the path, and appearing as the confused individual wondering where the path leads.

blocks.text: An astonishing amount of work for one woman.
blocks.directed: An astonishing amount of work for one woman.

blocks.text: But apparently infinite power does have its advantages.
blocks.directed: But apparently infinite power does have its advantages.
